19.5.m: He sings on the Bṛhatī verse addressed to Indra.

19.5.s: sam̐śravase viśravase satyaśravase śravase \\ iti sarve nidhanamupayanti //
19.5.d: सम्̐श्रवसे विश्रवसे सत्यश्रवसे श्रवसे \\ इति सर्वे निधनमुपयन्ति ॥
19.5.m: All join in the finale with "For renown, for wide renown, for true renown, for renown!"

19.5.s: saṃjityai vijityai satyajityai jityai \\ iti kṣatriyasya //
19.5.d: संजित्यै विजित्यै सत्यजित्यै जित्यै \\ इति क्षत्रियस्य ॥
19.5.m: [The finale] for a Kṣatriya is: "For conquest, for complete conquest, for true conquest, for conquest!"

19.5.s: sampuṣṭyai vipuṣṭyai satyapuṣṭyai puṣṭyai \\ iti vaiśyasya //
19.5.d: सम्पुष्ट्यै विपुष्ट्यै सत्यपुष्ट्यै पुष्ट्यै \\ इति वैश्यस्य ॥
19.5.m: [The finale] for a Vaiśya is: "For prosperity, for abundant prosperity, for true prosperity, for prosperity!"
Or as traditionally handed down for all.
With "Three gods...", he offers at the end of the recitation.

19.5.s: śeṣam ṛtvijaḥ prāṇabhakṣaṃ bhakṣayanti prāṇapā me \\ iti //
19.5.d: शेषम् ऋत्विजः प्राणभक्षं भक्षयन्ति प्राणपा मे \\ इति ॥
19.5.m: The officiating priests consume the remainder by inhaling, with "Protector of breath..."
The sacrificer consumes it directly with "The hairs are the effort..."

19.5.s: sviṣṭakṛtprabhṛty ā barhirhomāt kṛtvā parisrutkṣīraliptāny ādāyāvabhṛthavad gamanam //
19.5.d: स्विष्टकृत्प्रभृत्य् आ बर्हिर्होमात् कृत्वा परिस्रुत्क्षीरलिप्तान्य् आदायावभृथवद् गमनम् ॥
19.5.m: Having performed [the rites] from the Sviṣṭakṛt oblation up to the offering of sacrificial grass, taking the [vessels] smeared with liquor and milk, the departure [takes place] as in the concluding bath.
Having performed up to the addressing of the spit, [the procedure is that] of the concluding bath rite, beginning with standing in the water.
He sets the jar of māsara floating with "What the gods..."

19.5.s: sumitriyā nas \\ ity apo 'ñjalinādāya durmitriyās \\ iti dveṣyaṃ pariṣiñcati dvau vikramā udaṅ gatvā //
19.5.d: सुमित्रिया नस् \\ इत्य् अपो ऽञ्जलिनादाय दुर्मित्रियास् \\ इति द्वेष्यं परिषिञ्चति द्वौ विक्रमा उदङ् गत्वा ॥
19.5.m: Taking water in his cupped hands with "Friendly to us...", having walked two steps northward, he pours it around the hated enemy with "Unfriendly..."

19.5.s: avabhṛthavat snātvā vāso 'pāsanam \\ drupadād iva \\ iti //
19.5.d: अवभृथवत् स्नात्वा वासो ऽपासनम् \\ द्रुपदाद् इव \\ इति ॥
19.5.m: Having bathed as in the concluding bath, the casting off of the garment is done with "As if from a wooden post..."
The stepping out and the return are as in the soma [sacrifice].
He attends upon the Āhavanīya fire with "The waters today..."

19.5.s: edho 'si \\ iti samidham ādāyāhavanīye 'bhyādadhāti samid asi \\ iti //
19.5.d: एधो ऽसि \\ इति समिधम् आदायाहवनीये ऽभ्यादधाति समिद् असि \\ इति ॥
19.5.m: Taking a kindling stick with "Thou art kindling...", he places it on the Āhavanīya fire with "Thou art a kindling stick..."
And he offers with "He turns together..."
Having broken up the camp, there is a curd offering to Mitra and Varuṇa.
At its conclusion, there is an animal sacrifice to Indra Vayodhas.

19.6.m: In the Sautrāmaṇī, the iṣṭis and animal sacrifices have distinct common procedures because of the difference of time.
There are seventeen kindling verses.
The two portions of clarified butter are the Vṛtra-slaying [verses].
Or they contain the word vṛdhant in the animal sacrifices, because they are modifications of the sāṃnāyya.
The two accompanying offerings are Virāj verses, because there is no specific instruction.
For Vasiṣṭhas and Śunakas, the Āprī hymn has Nārāśaṃsa.
The summonses for fore-offerings and after-offerings for the first and last [animal sacrifices] are those of the archetype rite.
Some say they are dedicated to Indra for the first, and dedicated to Vayodhas for the last.
‘Kindled is Indra...’ are the Āprī verses of the first.

19.6.s: yājyānuvākyāś ca vapāpuroḍāśapaśūnām āyātv indras \\ iti //
19.6.d: याज्यानुवाक्याश् च वपापुरोडाशपशूनाम् आयात्व् इन्द्रस् \\ इति ॥
19.6.m: And the offering and introductory verses for the omenta, cake-offerings, and animals begin with: ‘May Indra come...’

19.6.s: hotā yakṣat samidhāgnim iti prayājapraiṣās tripaśoḥ //
19.6.d: होता यक्षत् समिधाग्निम् इति प्रयाजप्रैषास् त्रिपशोः ॥
19.6.m: ‘May the Hotṛ sacrifice to Agni with fuel...’ are the summonses for the fore-offerings of the three-animal sacrifice.

19.6.s: āpriyaś ca samiddho agnir aśvinā \\ iti //
19.6.d: आप्रियश् च समिद्धो अग्निर् अश्विना \\ इति ॥
19.6.m: And the Āprī verses begin with: ‘Agni, being kindled, [the two Aśvins]...’

19.6.s: aśvinā havir iti tisro vapānāṃ yājyānuvākyāḥ //
19.6.d: अश्विना हविर् इति तिस्रो वपानां याज्यानुवाक्याः ॥
19.6.m: ‘O Aśvins, the offering...’ are the three offering and introductory verses for the omenta.

19.6.s: prathamām anūcya dvitīyā yājyā dvitīyām anūcya tṛtīyā yājyā tṛtīyām anūcya prathamā yājyā //
19.6.d: प्रथमाम् अनूच्य द्वितीया याज्या द्वितीयाम् अनूच्य तृतीया याज्या तृतीयाम् अनूच्य प्रथमा याज्या ॥
19.6.m: Having recited the first as introductory, the second is the offering verse; having recited the second as introductory, the third is the offering verse; having recited the third as introductory, the first is the offering verse.
‘He who to Indra...’ [are the verses] for the cakes, as before.
And ‘O Aśvins, with cows...’ [are the verses] for the sacrificial portions.

19.6.s: grahāṇām \\ yuvam̐ surāmam \\ putram iva \\ iti //
19.6.d: ग्रहाणाम् \\ युवम्̐ सुरामम् \\ पुत्रम् इव \\ इति ॥
19.6.m: For the cups, ‘You two [the liquor]...’ and ‘Like a son...’ [are the verses].

19.6.s: paśusviṣṭakṛtas \\ yasminn aśvāsas \\ ahāvy agne \\ iti //
19.6.d: पशुस्विष्टकृतस् \\ यस्मिन्न् अश्वासस् \\ अहाव्य् अग्ने \\ इति ॥
19.6.m: For the animal Sviṣṭakṛt, ‘In whom horses...’ and ‘It has been offered, O Agni...’ [are the verses].

19.6.s: hotā yakṣad aśvinau \\ iti trayo vapānāṃ praiṣā yathāliṅgam //
19.6.d: होता यक्षद् अश्विनौ \\ इति त्रयो वपानां प्रैषा यथालिङ्गम् ॥
19.6.m: ‘May the Hotṛ sacrifice to the two Aśvins...’ are the three summonses for the omenta, according to their characteristic marks.
The subsequent ones are for the sacrificial portions, according to their characteristic marks.
The last two are for Vanaspati and Sviṣṭakṛt.

19.6.s: pratigariṣyaty upaviṣṭe \\ adhvaryo śom̐sāva \\ ity āhūya //
19.6.d: प्रतिगरिष्यत्य् उपविष्टे \\ अध्वर्यो शोम्̐साव \\ इत्य् आहूय ॥
19.6.m: When [the priest] who is to respond has sat down, having addressed him with: ‘O Adhvaryu, let us two recite!’;

19.7.m: he recites the section: ‘O Aśvins, with brilliance...’

19.7.s: uttamām̐ śiṣṭvā prāṅ navamyā daśamyā vā trayā devās \\ iti //
19.7.d: उत्तमाम्̐ शिष्ट्वा प्राङ् नवम्या दशम्या वा त्रया देवास् \\ इति ॥
19.7.m: leaving the last verse, before the ninth or tenth [verse he recites]: ‘Three gods...’
In the final syllable, there is elision from the vowel onward during the Praṇava.
Some say it ends with the Praṇava on that [syllable].

19.7.s: aśvinā tejasā \\ aśvinā pibatām iti yājyānuvākye saśastrasya //
19.7.d: अश्विना तेजसा \\ अश्विना पिबताम् इति याज्यानुवाक्ये सशस्त्रस्य ॥
19.7.m: ‘O Aśvins, with brilliance...’ and ‘O Aśvins, drink...’ are the offering and introductory verses for the [offering] accompanied by a recitation.
Having combined the summons for the introductory recitation [and the offering summons], the summonses for the after-offerings are: ‘The divine sacrificial grass...’
‘Agni today...’ is the summons for the Sūktavāka.
From the Sūktavāka onward, before the Avabhṛtha offering, it follows the archetype rite.

19.7.s: imaṃ me \ tat tvā \\ ity ekakapālasya //
19.7.d: इमं मे \ तत् त्वा \\ इत्य् एककपालस्य ॥
19.7.m: ‘This my [call]...’ and ‘That of you...’ are for the single-potsherd cake.

19.7.s: agnīvaruṇayos tvaṃ naḥ \ sa tvam iti //
19.7.d: अग्नीवरुणयोस् त्वं नः \ स त्वम् इति ॥
19.7.m: For Agni and Varuṇa, ‘You to us...’ and ‘He, you...’ [are the verses].

19.7.s: ādityasya sutrāmāṇam \\ mahīm ū ṣu mātaram iti //
19.7.d: आदित्यस्य सुत्रामाणम् \\ महीम् ऊ षु मातरम् इति ॥
19.7.m: For Āditya, ‘The good protector...’ and ‘The great mother indeed...’ [are the verses].

19.7.s: ā naḥ \ pra bāhavā \\ iti payasyāyāḥ //
19.7.d: आ नः \ प्र बाहवा \\ इति पयस्यायाः ॥
19.7.m: ‘To us...’ and ‘Forth arms...’ are for the curdled milk.
For the Vājina offering, ‘May it be well for us...’ and ‘In every battle...’ [are the verses].
The Āprī verses for Vayodhas are: ‘Agni, being kindled, with fuel...’

19.7.s: yājyānuvākyāś ca vapāpuroḍāśapaśūnām \\ vasantena ṛtunā \\ iti //
19.7.d: याज्यानुवाक्याश् च वपापुरोडाशपशूनाम् \\ वसन्तेन ऋतुना \\ इति ॥
19.7.m: And the offering and introductory verses for the omenta, cake-offerings, and animals are: ‘With the spring season...’

20.1.m: The Aśvamedha is a royal sacrifice for one who desires all.
On the eighth or ninth [lunar day] of the bright half of Phālguna [it begins].

20.1.s: brahmaudanaṃ pacati caturṇāṃ pātrāṇām añjaliprasṛtānāṃ ca //
20.1.d: ब्रह्मौदनं पचति चतुर्णां पात्राणाम् अञ्जलिप्रसृतानां च ॥
20.1.m: He cooks the Brahmā-rice of four vessels, and scooped with cupped hands.
Having anointed it, he presents it to the four principal officiating priests.

20.1.s: tebhyaś catvāri sahasrāṇi dadāti śatamānāṃś ca tāvataḥ //
20.1.d: तेभ्यश् चत्वारि सहस्राणि ददाति शतमानांश् च तावतः ॥
20.1.m: To them he gives four thousand [cows] and as many gold pieces.

20.1.s: aktvājyaśeṣeṇa raśanāṃ dvādaśāratniṃ trayodaśāratniṃ vā nidadhāti //
20.1.d: अक्त्वाज्यशेषेण रशनां द्वादशारत्निं त्रयोदशारत्निं वा निदधाति ॥
20.1.m: Having anointed the halter of twelve cubits or thirteen cubits with the remainder of clarified butter, he deposits it.

20.1.d: निष्कं प्रतिमुञ्चन् वाचयति तेजो ऽसि \\ इति ॥
20.1.m: Fastening a gold ornament [upon the sacrificer], he causes him to recite: ‘You are brilliance...’
The restraint of speech lasts until the granting of boons.

20.1.s: patnyaś cāyanty alaṅkṛtā niṣkiṇyo mahiṣī vāvātā parivṛktā pālāgalī sānucaryaḥ śatenásatena //
20.1.d: पत्न्यश् चायन्त्य् अलङ्कृता निष्किण्यो महिषी वावाता परिवृक्ता पालागली सानुचर्यः शतेन्áसतेन ॥
20.1.m: And the wives arrive, adorned and wearing golden ornaments: the chief queen (mahiṣī), the favorite wife (vāvātā), the discarded wife (parivṛktā), and the lowly wife (pālāgalī), accompanied by female attendants, a hundred for each.
Daughters of kings [are the attendants] of the first.
[Daughters] of nobles [are the attendants] of the second.
[Daughters] of charioteers and village headmen [are the attendants] of the third.
[Daughters] of chamberlains and charioteers [are the attendants] of the fourth.

20.1.s: agnyādheyavat praviśya hute 'gnihotre 'pareṇa gārhapatyam udakśirāḥ saṃviśati //
20.1.d: अग्न्याधेयवत् प्रविश्य हुते ऽग्निहोत्रे ऽपरेण गार्हपत्यम् उदक्शिराः संविशति ॥
20.1.m: Having entered as at the establishment of the sacred fires, after the agnihotra has been offered, he lies down to the west of the Gārhapatya fire with his head to the north.
A student of sacred lore (brahmacārin) [lies down] between the thighs of the favorite wife.
When the morning oblation has been offered, at the end of the full-spoon oblation, the granting of a boon [is given] to the Brahman priest.
And to the Adhvaryu priest, the golden ornament fastened [around his neck].
A sacrificial cake is [offered] to Agni Pathikṛt.
The sacrificial gift is a piece of gold weighing one hundred mānas.
Elsewhere too, when gold is measured [it is of this weight].
He dispenses a mess of cooked grain for Pūṣan.

20.1.s: devasya tvā \\ iti raśanām ādāya brahmann aśvaṃ bhantsyāmi \\ ity āha //
20.1.d: देवस्य त्वा \\ इति रशनाम् आदाय ब्रह्मन्न् अश्वं भन्त्स्यामि \\ इत्य् आह ॥
20.1.m: Taking the halter with 'At the instigation of the divine Savitṛ...', he says: 'O Brahman priest, I shall bind the horse.'

20.1.s: taṃ badhāna \\ iti brahmānujñātas \\ abhidhā asi \\ iti badhnāty aśvam //
20.1.d: तं बधान \\ इति ब्रह्मानुज्ञातस् \\ अभिधा असि \\ इति बध्नात्य् अश्वम् ॥
20.1.m: Authorized by the Brahman priest with 'Bind it', he binds the horse with 'Thou art the halter...'
[The horse should be] of three colors, or of all colors.
Black on the fore-body and white on the hind-body.

20.1.s: sthāvarā apo gatvā prajāpataye tvā \\ iti prokṣaty aśvaṃ pratimantram //
20.1.d: स्थावरा अपो गत्वा प्रजापतये त्वा \\ इति प्रोक्षत्य् अश्वं प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
20.1.m: Having gone to standing waters, he sprinkles the horse with each mantra: 'Thee for Prajāpati...'

20.1.s: āyogavam āha śvānaṃ caturakṣam abhimanyasva \\ iti //
20.1.d: आयोगवम् आह श्वानं चतुरक्षम् अभिमन्यस्व \\ इति ॥
20.1.m: He says to an Āyogava: 'Curse the four-eyed dog!'
He kills it with a pestle of sidhraka wood.

20.2.m: He makes [him] recite: 'He who against the steed...'

20.2.d: वेतसकटेनाधो ऽश्वं प्लावयति परो मर्तस् \\ इति ॥
20.2.m: He makes [the dog] float under the horse on a mat of reeds, with: 'Away is the mortal...'

20.2.s: agnisamīpam ānīya \\ agnaye svāhā \\ iti juhoty anuvākena pratimantram //
20.2.d: अग्निसमीपम् आनीय \\ अग्नये स्वाहा \\ इति जुहोत्य् अनुवाकेन प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
20.2.m: Having brought [the horse] near the fire, he offers [oblations] with the section 'To Agni svāhā...', mantra by mantra.
Or until the horse's neighing ceases.

20.2.s: dvādaśakapālān nirvapati bhinnatantrāñ chatamānadakṣiṇān madhyamasya rājataḥ savitre prasavitre savitra āsavitre savitre satyaprasavāya \\ iti //
20.2.d: द्वादशकपालान् निर्वपति भिन्नतन्त्राञ् छतमानदक्षिणान् मध्यमस्य राजतः सवित्रे प्रसवित्रे सवित्र आसवित्रे सवित्रे सत्यप्रसवाय \\ इति ॥
20.2.m: He dispenses [offerings of cakes] on twelve potsherds, having distinct common procedures, with a hundred mānas [of gold] as sacrificial gift, [and] for the middle one silver, to Savitṛ the stimulator, to Savitṛ the impeller, to Savitṛ of true instigation.

20.2.s: prayājeṣu dakṣiṇato brāhmaṇo yajamānasya yajñadānayuktāḥ svayaṃkrtās tisro gāthā gāyaty uttaramandrāyām //
20.2.d: प्रयाजेषु दक्षिणतो ब्राह्मणो यजमानस्य यज्ञदानयुक्ताः स्वयंक्र्तास् तिस्रो गाथा गायत्य् उत्तरमन्द्रायाम् ॥
20.2.m: During the preliminary offerings (prayājas), to the south, a Brāhmaṇa sings in the uttaramandrā note three self-composed verses connected with the sacrificer's sacrifices and gifts.
A noble [sings verses] connected with battles and victories during the dhṛti oblations.

20.2.s: adhvaryuyajamānau dakṣiṇe 'śvakarṇe japatas \\ vibhūr mātrā \\ iti //
20.2.d: अध्वर्युयजमानौ दक्षिणे ऽश्वकर्णे जपतस् \\ विभूर् मात्रा \\ इति ॥
20.2.m: The Adhvaryu priest and the sacrificer whisper into the right ear of the horse: 'Thou art a broad ruler by thy measure...'
The releasing is performed as in an animal sacrifice, amidst a hundred gelded horses.

20.2.s: devā āśāpālās \\ iti rakṣiṇo 'syādiśatyanucarījñātīyāṃs tāvatastāvataḥ kavaciniṣaṅgikalāpidaṇḍino yathāsaṃkhyam //
20.2.d: देवा आशापालास् \\ इति रक्षिणो ऽस्यादिशत्यनुचरीज्ञातीयांस् तावतस्तावतः कवचिनिषङ्गिकलापिदण्डिनो यथासंख्यम् ॥
20.2.m: With 'Ye gods who guard the regions...', he assigns its guards, the kinsmen of the female attendants, in equal numbers: wearing armor, bearing quivers, bearing bows, and holding staves, respectively.

20.2.d: ब्राह्मणो ऽश्वमेधे ऽविद्वान् वृत्तिः स वः ॥
20.2.m: 'A Brāhmaṇa ignorant of the horse-sacrifice is your livelihood.'
And dwelling in the houses of chariot-makers.

20.2.s: abhiṣekyā bhaviṣyata samāpnuvantas \\ ity āha rājaputrān //
20.2.d: अभिषेक्या भविष्यत समाप्नुवन्तस् \\ इत्य् आह राजपुत्रान् ॥
20.2.m: 'May you who are to be consecrated attain [kingship]!' he says to the royal princes.
To the south of the altar, they sit upon golden seats.
The Adhvaryu priest and the sacrificer [sit] on two bunches of grass.
The Hotṛ priest, the Brahman priest, and the Udgātṛ priest [sit] on cushions.

20.2.s: hotar bhūtāny ācakṣva \ bhūteṣv imaṃ yajamānam adhyūha \\ iti //
20.2.d: होतर् भूतान्य् आचक्ष्व \ भूतेष्व् इमं यजमानम् अध्यूह \\ इति ॥
20.2.m: 'O Hotṛ priest, narrate the beings; place this sacrificer among the beings!'

20.3.s: havai hotar iti pratigṛṇāti tadante preṣyati vīṇāgaṇagino rājarṣibhir yajamānam̐ saṃgāyata \\ iti //
20.3.d: हवै होतर् इति प्रतिगृणाति तदन्ते प्रेष्यति वीणागणगिनो राजर्षिभिर् यजमानम्̐ संगायत \\ इति ॥
20.3.m: With 'Yes, O Hotṛ', he responds; at the end of that, he orders the lute-players: 'Sing together of the sacrificer along with the royal sages!'

20.3.s: dakṣiṇāgnau juhoti hiṅkārāya svāhā \\ iti prakramān //
20.3.d: दक्षिणाग्नौ जुहोति हिङ्काराय स्वाहा \\ इति प्रक्रमान् ॥
20.3.m: In the Dakṣiṇāgni fire, he offers the steps with 'To the sound hiṅ, svāhā!'

20.3.s: āhavanīye 'stamite catasro dhṛtīr iha rantir iti //
20.3.d: आहवनीये ऽस्तमिते चतस्रो धृतीर् इह रन्तिर् इति ॥
20.3.m: In the Āhavanīya fire at sunset, [he offers] the four dhṛti oblations with 'Here is delight...'
The lying down with the favorite wife, the offerings to Savitṛ, the singing in the uttaramandrā note, the revolving cycle of tales, and the dhṛti oblations [continue] for a year.
And some [say they last] half a month, a month, three months, or six months.
He gives a hundred [cows] each to the two lute-singers.
The singing together [of the sacrificer] with the royal sages continues up to the preparatory rite (dīkṣaṇīyā).
From the end of the consecration up to the day of preparation (aupavasathya), [the singing is] together with the gods.
At the beginning of [the offering of] the animal [victims], [he sings] with Prajāpati during the soma pressings.
The sacrifice for the horse’s misfortunes consists of pots of boiled rice (caru) at the conclusion of the Sāvitra [oblations].
If it has an incurable or violent disease, [a cake] baked on potsherds of earth dedicated to Agni Vaiśvānara.
Jātūkarṇya says: on potsherds made of clay clods, because of the breakage.

20.3.s: nāśe tantreṇa dyāvāpṛthivyaḥ payo vāyavyam̐ sauryaḥ //
20.3.d: नाशे तन्त्रेण द्यावापृथिव्यः पयो वायव्यम्̐ सौर्यः ॥
20.3.m: If it disappears, [there are offered] combined into a single procedure: milk dedicated to Dyāvāpṛthivī, [milk] dedicated to Vāyu, and [a caru] dedicated to Sūrya.

20.4.m: he performs taking the halter and the other [rites] connected with the horse for another [horse].

20.4.s: paścālambhanādy ādhvaradīkṣāṇīyāyāḥ kṛtvā catvāry audgrabhaṇāni juhoty ādhvarikāṇi //
20.4.d: पश्चालम्भनाद्य् आध्वरदीक्षाणीयायाः कृत्वा चत्वार्य् औद्ग्रभणानि जुहोत्य् आध्वरिकाणि ॥
20.4.m: Having performed [the rites] from the post-touching onward belonging to the dīkṣaṇīyā of the soma sacrifice, he offers the four audgrabhaṇa oblations of the soma sacrifice,
and three belonging to the horse sacrifice with [the mantra]: 'To Ka svāhā!'

20.4.s: adhvaradīkṣaṇīyāyāś catvāri trīṇi trīṇi cāśvam adhikāni kṛṣṇājināntam anvaham //
20.4.d: अध्वरदीक्षणीयायाश् चत्वारि त्रीणि त्रीणि चाश्वम् अधिकानि कृष्णाजिनान्तम् अन्वहम् ॥
20.4.m: he offers day after day up to the black antelope skin [rite] the four [audgrabhaṇa oblations] of the soma sacrifice’s dīkṣaṇīyā and the three additional ones of the horse sacrifice.
He observes the standard observance, because it has not [yet] been observed.
And on the seventh day he distributes [the oblations] belonging to the Fire-altar building.
He performs [the rites] beginning with anointing.
There are six [oblations] belonging to the Fire-altar in place of the four.
The tenth is with [the verse]: 'Of the divine Savitṛ, every...'

20.4.s: kṛṣṇājinādy ā samidādhānāt kṛtvā \\ ā brahman \\ iti japati //
20.4.d: कृष्णाजिनाद्य् आ समिदाधानात् कृत्वा \\ आ ब्रह्मन् \\ इति जपति ॥
20.4.m: Having performed [the rites] beginning with the black antelope skin up to the placing of fuel sticks, he mutters: 'May there be born in the Brahman...'
There are twelve consecration days and [twelve] Upasad days.
The sacrificial ground should have constant water to the east.

20.4.d: आद्यो ऽग्निर् द्विगुणस् त्रिगुण एकविम्̐शतिविधो वा ॥
20.4.m: The first Fire-altar is double [the size], threefold, or twenty-one-fold.
There are twenty-one sacrificial posts, like the group of eleven.
There are six each of Bilva, Khadira, and Palāśa.
At each sacrificial post there is an animal victim dedicated to Agni-Soma.
The animal victims of the pressing day form two groups of eleven.

20.4.s: vijayamadhyād dhotuḥ prācī dig dakṣiṇā brahmaṇo 'dhvaryoḥ pratīcy udgātur udīcī //
20.4.d: विजयमध्याद् धोतुः प्राची दिग् दक्षिणा ब्रह्मणो ऽध्वर्योः प्रतीच्य् उद्गातुर् उदीची ॥
20.4.m: From the center of conquest, the eastern direction [of the realm] belongs to the Hotṛ, the southern to the Brahman, the western to the Adhvaryu, and the northern to the Udgātṛ.
He gives a third each day, excluding the land, the men, and the property of Brāhmaṇas.
At the third pressing, having drawn the Ukthya cup, at the time of the Āgnimāruta śastra he divides it threefold.
Corresponding to those cups are the offering and the consumption.
Having repeatedly drawn the Vasatīvarī waters, having poured them together in each direction, he carries them around.

20.4.s: ājyasaktudhānālājānām ekaikaṃ juhoti prāṇāya svāhā \\ iti pratimantram̐ sarvarātram āvartam //
20.4.d: आज्यसक्तुधानालाजानाम् एकैकं जुहोति प्राणाय स्वाहा \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम्̐ सर्वरात्रम् आवर्तम् ॥
20.4.m: Throughout the whole night, in rotation, he offers one [portion] each of ghee, parched grain meal, roasted grains, and fried grains with each mantra: 'To Prāṇa svāhā!'
With 'To the dawn [svāhā]' when it dawns.

20.5.s: mahimānau gṛhṇāti sauvarṇena pūrvam \\ hiraṇyagarbhas \\ iti dvitīyam̐ rājatena yaḥ prāṇatas \\ iti //
20.5.d: महिमानौ गृह्णाति सौवर्णेन पूर्वम् \\ हिरण्यगर्भस् \\ इति द्वितीयम्̐ राजतेन यः प्राणतस् \\ इति ॥
20.5.m: He draws the two Mahimān cups: the first with a golden [vessel] using 'The Golden Embryo...', the second with a silver [vessel] using 'He who is the giver of breath...'
The creeping toward the Bahiṣpavamāna chant takes place while holding on to the horse.
He shows it a mare; it neighs, [and] that is its chant.
With the horse they cause [the ground] of the Āstāva to be stepped upon.
Having dedicated the animals of the set of eleven and the horse and others,
He yokes it with: 'They yoke the tawny [steed]...'
And the other [horses] with: 'They yoke his...'

20.5.s: apo yātvāvagāḍheṣu vācayati yad vātas \\ iti //
20.5.d: अपो यात्वावगाढेषु वाचयति यद् वातस् \\ इति ॥
20.5.m: Having driven to the water, when they have stepped into it, he makes [the sacrificer] recite: 'What the wind...'

20.5.s: āyāya vimuktam aśvaṃ mahiṣī vāvātā parivṛktājyenābhyañjanti pūrvakāyamadhyāparakāyān yathādeśam \\ vasavas tvā \\ iti pratimantram //
20.5.d: आयाय विमुक्तम् अश्वं महिषी वावाता परिवृक्ताज्येनाभ्यञ्जन्ति पूर्वकायमध्यापरकायान् यथादेशम् \\ वसवस् त्वा \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
20.5.m: When [the horse] has returned and been unharnessed, the chief queen, the favourite wife, and the discarded wife anoint the horse with ghee—the fore-body, the middle, and the hindquarters respectively according to their places—with the mantras beginning 'May the Vasus [anoint] you', one mantra for each.

20.5.s: abhram̐śyamānān maṇīnt sauvarṇān ekaśatamekaśataṃ kesarāpucheṣv āvayanti bhūr bhuvaḥ svar iti pratimahāvyāhṛti //
20.5.d: अभ्रम्̐श्यमानान् मणीन्त् सौवर्णान् एकशतमेकशतं केसरापुछेष्व् आवयन्ति भूर् भुवः स्वर् इति प्रतिमहाव्याहृति ॥
20.5.m: They weave one hundred and one gold beads that do not fall off into its mane and tail, with the Great Utterances 'bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ', one for each.
According to some, the female attendants also [weave beads] silently.

20.5.s: aśvāya rātrihutaśeṣaṃ prayachati lājī3ñ chācī3n iti //
20.5.d: अश्वाय रात्रिहुतशेषं प्रयछति लाजी3ञ् छाची3न् इति ॥
20.5.m: He offers the remnant of the night offering to the horse, with: 'Lājī3n śācī3n...'.
If it does not eat, [there is] casting it into the waters.

20.5.s:
brahmā pṛchati hotāraṃ yūpam abhitaḥ kaḥ svid ekākī \\ iti //
sūryas \\ ity ācaṣṭe //
20.5.d:
ब्रह्मा पृछति होतारं यूपम् अभितः कः स्विद् एकाकी \\ इति ॥
सूर्यस् \\ इत्य् आचष्टे ॥
20.5.m: Near the sacrificial post, the Brahman priest asks the Hotṛ priest: 'Who indeed wanders alone?'; he answers: 'The sun'.

20.5.s: hotā brahmāṇam \\ kā svid āsīt \\ iti //
20.5.d: होता ब्रह्माणम् \\ का स्विद् आसीत् \\ इति ॥
20.5.m: The Hotṛ priest [asks] the Brahman priest: 'What indeed was [the first conception]?'

20.6.m: He performs the churning of fire and the subsequent rites.
To the central post facing the fire he binds the horse, the hornless he-goat, and the wild ox.
The deities of the horse and the others are as prescribed.
[He binds] fifteen [tame animals] each, beginning with the red deer and ending with those sacred to Sūrya, to the other [posts].
[He binds] thirteen [wild animals] each, beginning with the francolin partridges and ending with the spotted ones, between the sacrificial posts.

20.6.s: aśvaprokṣaṇam adbhyas tvā \ vāyuṣ ṭvā \\ iti //
20.6.d: अश्वप्रोक्षणम् अद्भ्यस् त्वा \ वायुष् ट्वा \\ इति ॥
20.6.m: The sprinkling of the horse is with: 'To the waters, you...', 'May Vāyu [protect] you...'.

20.6.s: upagṛhṇāti \\ apāṃ perur \ agniḥ paśur iti //
20.6.d: उपगृह्णाति \\ अपां पेरुर् \ अग्निः पशुर् इति ॥
20.6.m: He takes hold [of it] with: 'The drinker of the waters...', 'Agni is the animal...'
They release the francolin partridges and the others after carrying fire around them.
The suffocation of the horse takes place upon a gold cloth and upper garments.

20.6.s: paripaśavye hutvā prāṇāya svāhā \\ iti tisro 'parāḥ //
20.6.d: परिपशव्ये हुत्वा प्राणाय स्वाहा \\ इति तिस्रो ऽपराः ॥
20.6.m: Having offered the oblations regarding the animals, he offers three subsequent oblations with: 'To the out-breath, svāhā...'

20.6.s: vācayati patnīr nayan namas te \\ ambe \\ iti //
20.6.d: वाचयति पत्नीर् नयन् नमस् ते \\ अम्बे \\ इति ॥
20.6.m: Leading the wives, he makes them recite: 'Homage to you...', 'O mother...'

20.6.s: aśvaṃ tristriḥ pariyanti pitṛvan madhye gaṇānām \\ priyāṇām \\ nidhīnām iti //
20.6.d: अश्वं त्रिस्त्रिः परियन्ति पितृवन् मध्ये गणानाम् \\ प्रियाणाम् \\ निधीनाम् इति ॥
20.6.m: They walk around the horse three times each, like the rite for the Fathers, reciting in the middle: 'Of the troops...', 'Of the dear ones...', 'Of the treasures...'

20.6.s: prakṣāliteṣu mahiṣyaśvam upasṃviśati \\ āham ajāni \\ iti //
20.6.d: प्रक्षालितेषु महिष्यश्वम् उपस्ंविशति \\ आहम् अजानि \\ इति ॥
20.6.m: When they have washed [the horse], the chief queen lies down beside the horse, reciting: 'I will urge...'
He covers [them] with an upper garment, reciting: 'In the heavenly world...'

20.6.s: aśvaśiśnam upasthe kurute vṛṣā vājī \\ iti //
20.6.d: अश्वशिश्नम् उपस्थे कुरुते वृषा वाजी \\ इति ॥
20.6.m: She places the horse's penis upon her lap, reciting: 'The vigorous seed-pourer...'

20.6.d: उत् सक्थ्यास् \\ इत्य् अश्वं यजमानो ऽभिमन्त्रयते ॥
20.6.m: With 'Raise the thighs...', the sacrificer addresses the horse.

20.6.s: adhvaryubrahmodgātṛhotṛkṣattāraḥ kumārīpatnībhiḥ saṃvadante yakāsakau \\ iti daśarcasya dvābhyāṃdvābhyām \\ hayehaye 'sau \\ ity āmantryāmantrya //
20.6.d: अध्वर्युब्रह्मोद्गातृहोतृक्षत्तारः कुमारीपत्नीभिः संवदन्ते यकासकौ \\ इति दशर्चस्य द्वाभ्यांद्वाभ्याम् \\ हयेहये ऽसौ \\ इत्य् आमन्त्र्यामन्त्र्य ॥
20.6.m: The Adhvaryu priest, the Brahman priest, the Udgātṛ priest, the Hotṛ priest, and the carver engage in abusive dialogue with the maiden and the wives with two verses each of the ten-verse hymn, having repeatedly hailed them with: 'Hey, hey, such a one!'

20.6.s: mahiṣīm utthāpya puruṣās \\ dadhikrāvṇas \\ ity āhuḥ //
20.6.d: महिषीम् उत्थाप्य पुरुषास् \\ दधिक्राव्णस् \\ इत्य् आहुः ॥
20.6.m: Having made the chief queen rise, the men recite: 'Of Dadhikrāvan...'

20.7.s: tisraḥ patnyo 'sipathān kalpayanty aśvasya sūcībhir lauharājatasauvarṇībhir maṇisaṃkhyābhir gāyatrī triṣṭub iti dvābhyāṃdvābhyām //
20.7.d: तिस्रः पत्न्यो ऽसिपथान् कल्पयन्त्य् अश्वस्य सूचीभिर् लौहराजतसौवर्णीभिर् मणिसंख्याभिर् गायत्री त्रिष्टुब् इति द्वाभ्यांद्वाभ्याम् ॥
20.7.m: The three wives mark the paths for the knife on the horse with copper, silver, and gold needles corresponding in number to the beads, with two verses each: 'The Gāyatrī...', 'The Triṣṭubh...'
Or with silver, gold, and lead [needles], because of the mention in the mantras.

20.7.s: aśvaṃ viśāsty anuvākena kas tvā chyati \\ iti //
20.7.d: अश्वं विशास्त्य् अनुवाकेन कस् त्वा छ्यति \\ इति ॥
20.7.m: He carves the horse with the section: 'Who cuts you?...'
They take out its fat for the purpose of the omentum.

20.7.s: prājāpatyavapānām uttarataḥ śrapaṇam̐ homo haviṣaś ca //
20.7.d: प्राजापत्यवपानाम् उत्तरतः श्रपणम्̐ होमो हविषश् च ॥
20.7.m: The cooking and the offering of the omenta and the sacrificial substance for Prajāpati take place on the north.

20.7.s: prāg vapāhomād dhotādhvaryū ca sadasi saṃvadete catasṛbhiḥ kaḥ svid ekākī \\ iti pūrvavat //
20.7.d: प्राग् वपाहोमाद् धोताध्वर्यू च सदसि संवदेते चतसृभिः कः स्विद् एकाकी \\ इति पूर्ववत् ॥
20.7.m: Before the offering of the omentum, the Hotṛ priest and the Adhvaryu priest engage in dialogue in the Sadas with four verses: 'Who indeed wanders alone?...', as before.
And the Brahman priest and the Udgātṛ priest [converse], with: 'I ask you...'

20.7.s: punaḥ pūrvāv apareṇottaravedim \\ kā svid āsīt \\ iti //
20.7.d: पुनः पूर्वाव् अपरेणोत्तरवेदिम् \\ का स्विद् आसीत् \\ इति ॥
20.7.m: Again, the former two [converse] west of the high altar, with: 'What indeed was [the first conception]?...'
And the latter two [converse], with: 'How many [parts] of this?...'
The sacrificer [asks] the Adhvaryu priest: 'I ask you...'

20.7.s: sarvahutena mahimnā carati yas te 'han \\ iti juhoti //
20.7.d: सर्वहुतेन महिम्ना चरति यस् ते ऽहन् \\ इति जुहोति ॥
20.7.m: He proceeds with the Mahiman cup offered entirely; he offers it with: 'That which by day...'
[The animals are] a goat, an ox, and a ram, in accordance with the characteristic marks of the names of the animals.
Because the prescriptive word expresses a quality.
According to some, immediately following are twenty-one offerings to the deities of the Four-Month sacrifices, excluding those to the Fathers, the Tryambaka rites, and the repetitions.
According to some, [they are dedicated] to Indrāgnī, the Viśvedevas, and Ka.

20.7.s: vapānte dvitīyena pūrvavat \\ yas te rātrau \\ iti juhoti //
20.7.d: वपान्ते द्वितीयेन पूर्ववत् \\ यस् ते रात्रौ \\ इति जुहोति ॥
20.7.m: At the end of the omentum [offering], he offers with the second [Mahiman cup] as before, with: 'That which by night...'
Having performed [the rites] from the gliding forth up to the setting down of the animal;

20.8.m: he portions out the blood in the windpipe of the wild ox and the hoof of the horse into an iron pot.
[The portions] of the animals for Prajāpati [are placed] on reed branches.

20.8.s: sviṣṭakṛdvanaspatyantare śūlyam̐ hutvā devatāśvāṅgebhyo juhoti \\ amuṣmai svāhā \\ iti pratidevatam̐ śādaprabhṛtitvagantebhyaḥ //
20.8.d: स्विष्टकृद्वनस्पत्यन्तरे शूल्यम्̐ हुत्वा देवताश्वाङ्गेभ्यो जुहोति \\ अमुष्मै स्वाहा \\ इति प्रतिदेवतम्̐ शादप्रभृतित्वगन्तेभ्यः ॥
20.8.m: Between the Sviṣṭakṛt and the Vanaspati offerings, having offered the roasted flesh on a spit, he makes oblations to the deities of the horse's limbs with, "To so-and-so, svāhā," for each deity, beginning with the grass and ending with the skin.

20.8.s: mā no mitras \\ iti ca pratyṛcam anuvākābhyām //
20.8.d: मा नो मित्रस् \\ इति च प्रत्यृचम् अनुवाकाभ्याम् ॥
20.8.m: And verse by verse with the two anuvākas: "Let not Mitra..."
[He offers] the last [verse], addressed to Dyāvāpṛthivī.

20.8.s: sviṣṭakṛdante \\ agnibhyaḥ sviṣṭakṛdbhyaḥ svāhā \\ iti lohitaṃ juhoti yathāvattam //
20.8.d: स्विष्टकृदन्ते \\ अग्निभ्यः स्विष्टकृद्भ्यः स्वाहा \\ इति लोहितं जुहोति यथावत्तम् ॥
20.8.m: At the conclusion of the Sviṣṭakṛt offering, he offers the blood as apportioned, with: "To the Sviṣṭakṛt Agnis, svāhā."
Or [he offers it] with a horse's hoof at the conclusion of the after-offerings.
With an iron vessel at the conclusion of the Patnīsaṃyājas.

20.8.s: imā nu kam iti ca dvipadāḥ //
20.8.d: इमा नु कम् इति च द्विपदाः ॥
20.8.m: And the two-verse lines: "Now indeed..."

20.8.s: sarvastomo jyotir gaur āyur abhijid viśvajin mahāvratam aptoryāmo vā //
20.8.d: सर्वस्तोमो ज्योतिर् गौर् आयुर् अभिजिद् विश्वजिन् महाव्रतम् अप्तोर्यामो वा ॥
20.8.m: Or [it is] a Sarvastoma, a Jyotis, a Gauḥ, an Āyus, an Abhijit, a Viśvajit, a Mahāvrata, or an Aptoryāma.
In the Aptoryāma, the night round is subsequent to the Tiro'hnya cups.
And the two Prājāpatya [victims are bound] to the Agniṣṭha post.

20.8.s: avabhṛtheṣṭyante 'psu magnasya piṅgalakhalativiklidhaśuklasya mūrdhani juhoti jumbakāya svāhā \\ iti //
20.8.d: अवभृथेष्ट्यन्ते ऽप्सु मग्नस्य पिङ्गलखलतिविक्लिधशुक्लस्य मूर्धनि जुहोति जुम्बकाय स्वाहा \\ इति ॥
20.8.m: At the end of the purificatory bath offering, he offers upon the head of a brown-eyed, bald, white-spotted man immersed in water, with: "To Jumbaka, svāhā."

20.8.d: उत्क्रान्ते यजमाने पापकृतो ऽभ्यवयन्त्य् अचरित्वा व्रतानि ॥
20.8.m: When the sacrificer has stepped out, evil-doers descend [into the water] without having observed the observances.
They are called purified by the Aśvamedha.
[The procedure] of the first two ends with the striking together of the water jars.
Because in the remaining rites there is an absence of consecration observances.
There are twenty-one Anūbandhyā cows.
At the end of the Udavasānīyā offering, he gives the wives together with their female attendants, according to the agreement.
And the maiden and the Pālāgalī to the Adhvaryu.
Or only the female attendants, because the others have eligibility for the result [of the rite].
For twelve days there is a sacrificial cake for Agni.

20.8.s: pratyṛtu paśūn ālabhate ṣaṭṣaḍ vasantādy āgneyān aindrān pārjanyān mārutān vā maitrāvaruṇān aindravaiṣṇavān aindrābārhaspatyān //
20.8.d: प्रत्यृतु पशून् आलभते षट्षड् वसन्ताद्य् आग्नेयान् ऐन्द्रान् पार्जन्यान् मारुतान् वा मैत्रावरुणान् ऐन्द्रवैष्णवान् ऐन्द्राबार्हस्पत्यान् ॥
20.8.m: Season by season he immolates victims, six each, beginning in spring: [six] for Agni, [six] for Indra, [six] for Parjanya, or [six] for the Maruts, [six] for Mitrā-Varuṇā, [six] for Indrā-Viṣṇū, and [six] for Indrā-Bṛhaspatī.

21.1.m: The Puruṣamedha has twenty-three consecration days, for one who desires pre-eminence.
Between two Agniṣṭomas there is an Atirātra flanked by Ukthyas.
There is a set of eleven sacrificial posts.

21.1.s: paśūn upākariṣyann atirātre deva savitar iti pratyṛcaṃ tisro juhoti //
21.1.d: पशून् उपाकरिष्यन्न् अतिरात्रे देव सवितर् इति प्रत्यृचं तिस्रो जुहोति ॥
21.1.m: When about to bring up the victims on the Atirātra day, he offers three oblations verse by verse with: "God Savitṛ..."
Having brought up the eleven victims and the Brāhmaṇa and other human victims,
at the time of tying them, [he ties] the first forty-eight to the Agniṣṭha post;
eleven to each of the others;

21.1.s: niyuktān brahmābhiṣṭauti hotṛvad anuvākena sahasraśīrṣā \\ iti //
21.1.d: नियुक्तान् ब्रह्माभिष्टौति होतृवद् अनुवाकेन सहस्रशीर्षा \\ इति ॥
21.1.m: The Brahman priest praises the tied victims like the Hotṛ, with the anuvāka: "The thousand-headed..."
They release the Brāhmaṇa and other human victims like the Kapiñjala and other wild creatures.
Between the Sviṣṭakṛt and the Vanaspati offerings, he offers to the deities of the human victims.
The sacrificial gift is as in the Aśvamedha, along with the human victims.
All possessions [are given] by a Brāhmaṇa.
There are three Anūbandhyā cows for each deity, and five for the last.

21.1.s: traidhātavyante samārohyātmann agnī sūryam upasthāya \\ adbhyaḥ sambhṛtaḥ ity anuvākenānapekṣamāṇo 'raṇyaṃ gatvā na pratyeyāt //
21.1.d: त्रैधातव्यन्ते समारोह्यात्मन्न् अग्नी सूर्यम् उपस्थाय \\ अद्भ्यः सम्भृतः इत्य् अनुवाकेनानपेक्षमाणो ऽरण्यं गत्वा न प्रत्येयात् ॥
21.1.m: At the conclusion of the Traidhātavīyā offering, having mounted the fires into himself, having paid reverence to the sun with the anuvāka, "Brought together from the waters...," he should go to the forest without looking back and not return.
Or, if he intends to dwell in the village, [he mounts them] into the two churning sticks.

21.2.m: The Sarvamedha is for one who desires everything.

21.2.s: agniṣṭut traya ukthyā indrastut sūryastud vaiśvadevastut vājapeyo 'ptoryāmaḥ sarvam asminn ālabhate //
21.2.d: अग्निष्टुत् त्रय उक्थ्या इन्द्रस्तुत् सूर्यस्तुद् वैश्वदेवस्तुत् वाजपेयो ऽप्तोर्यामः सर्वम् अस्मिन्न् आलभते ॥
21.2.m: An Agniṣṭut, three Ukthyas, an Indrastut, a Sūryastut, a Vaiśvadevastut, a Vājapeya, and an Aptoryāma; in this he immolates everything.
He offers the skins of baked foods.
The cuttings of herbs and trees.
He offers every kind of food at the end of the omentum oblation;
and at the third soma pressing when the oblations have been offered.
The middle day of the Aśvamedha takes the place of the Vrata day.
That of the Puruṣamedha takes the place of the Vājapeya.
The two Ukthyas are a Triṇava and a Trayastriṃśa.
The sacrificial gift is as in the Puruṣamedha, including the land.

21.3.m: The Pitṛmedha is performed when the year is forgotten;

21.3.s: yāvanto dhuviṣyantaḥ syus tāvataḥ kumbhān ādāya chattrāṇi cāparimitāni //
21.3.d: यावन्तो धुविष्यन्तः स्युस् तावतः कुम्भान् आदाय छत्त्राणि चापरिमितानि ॥
21.3.m: Having taken as many jars as there will be persons shaking [the winnowing fans], and an unlimited number of umbrellas,

21.3.s: śarīrāṇi grāmasamīpam āhṛtya kumbhena talpe kṛtvāhatapakṣeṇa paritatyāyaseṣu vādyamāneṣu vīṇāyāṃ coddhatāyām amātyās tristriḥ parikrāmanty uttarīyair upavājanair vopavājayantaḥ //
21.3.d: शरीराणि ग्रामसमीपम् आहृत्य कुम्भेन तल्पे कृत्वाहतपक्षेण परितत्यायसेषु वाद्यमानेषु वीणायां चोद्धतायाम् अमात्यास् त्रिस्त्रिः परिक्रामन्त्य् उत्तरीयैर् उपवाजनैर् वोपवाजयन्तः ॥
21.3.m: having brought the bones near the village, placed them in a jar on a couch, surrounded [them] with unwashed cloth, while iron [instruments] are being beaten and a lute is loudly played, the relatives walk around three times each, fanning [them] with upper garments or fans;
And [they do so] in the early night, midnight, and the latter part of the night.
On this day, the food is devoid of solid grain;
and it is accompanied by dance, song, and musical instruments.
Some bring food near for him.
At dawn, taking the bones, they go toward the south,
so that as one performs [the rite], the sun rises;
on saline soil, sloping towards the north, or level;
and far from Nyagrodha, Aśvattha, Tilvaka, Haridru, Sphūrjaka, Bibhīdaka, and trees of inauspicious names;

21.3.s: grāmatas tejanīm uchritya na nyasyed gṛheṣūchrayet //
21.3.d: ग्रामतस् तेजनीम् उछ्रित्य न न्यस्येद् गृहेषूछ्रयेत् ॥
21.3.m: Having raised a reed shaft towards the village, he should not set it down; he should raise it in the houses.
He measures out a man's length with corners facing the cardinal directions;
broader to the north and to the west.
Having measured it out, he drives pegs into the corners:
a Palāśa peg in the east; Śamī, Vāraṇa, and wooden pegs in the others.

21.3.s: apasalavisṛṣṭayā rajjvā paritatya \\ apeto yantu \\ iti palāśaśākhayā vyudūhati //
21.3.d: अपसलविसृष्टया रज्ज्वा परितत्य \\ अपेतो यन्तु \\ इति पलाशशाखया व्युदूहति ॥
21.3.m: Having enclosed it with a cord spun counter-clockwise, he sweeps it out with a Palāśa branch with: 'Let them go away.'

21.3.s: dakṣiṇā śākhāṃ nirasya pariśridbhiḥ pariśrayati pūrvavad aparimitābhiḥ //
21.3.d: दक्षिणा शाखां निरस्य परिश्रिद्भिः परिश्रयति पूर्ववद् अपरिमिताभिः ॥
21.3.m: Having discarded the branch to the south, he encloses [it] with an unlimited number of enclosing stones, as before.

21.3.s: audumbarasīra uttarato vā ṣaḍgave yujyamāne yuṅkta \\ iti sampreṣya savitā te \\ iti japati //
21.3.d: औदुम्बरसीर उत्तरतो वा षड्गवे युज्यमाने युङ्क्त \\ इति सम्प्रेष्य सविता ते \\ इति जपति ॥
21.3.m: A plow of Udumbara wood, or to the north; while a team of six oxen is being yoked, having given the call: 'Yoke!', he mutters: 'May Savitṛ for you.'

21.4.s: anurajju catasraḥ sītāḥ kṛṣati vāyuḥ punātu \\ iti pratimantram //
21.4.d: अनुरज्जु चतस्रः सीताः कृषति वायुः पुनातु \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
21.4.m: Along the cord, he plows four furrows, with a mantra for each: 'May Vāyu purify.'
The first [furrow] is to the north, running west;
an unlimited number in the middle, silently.

21.4.s: anaḍuho vimucya vimucyantām iti dakṣiṇā sīra nirasya \\ aśvatthe vas \\ iti sarvauṣadhaṃ vapati //
21.4.d: अनडुहो विमुच्य विमुच्यन्ताम् इति दक्षिणा सीर निरस्य \\ अश्वत्थे वस् \\ इति सर्वौषधं वपति ॥
21.4.m: Having unyoked the oxen with: 'Let them be unyoked,' and cast the plow to the south, he sows all herbs with: 'In the Aśvattha, your [dwelling].'

21.4.s: savitā te \\ iti śarīrāṇi nivapati madhye //
21.4.d: सविता ते \\ इति शरीराणि निवपति मध्ये ॥
21.4.m: With: 'May Savitṛ for you,' he pours out the bones in the middle.

21.4.s: tūṣṇīm anyaḥ kumbham ākṣṇauti dakṣiṇānavānant sṛtvā //
21.4.d: तूष्णीम् अन्यः कुम्भम् आक्ष्णौति दक्षिणानवानन्त् सृत्वा ॥
21.4.m: Another person silently breaks the jar, having run towards the south without breathing out.
When he has returned, [the Adhvaryu] mutters: 'Far away, O Death.'

21.4.s: śaṃ vātas \\ iti yathāṅgaṃ kalpayitveṣṭakāṃ nidadhāti madhye tūṣṇīm //
21.4.d: शं वातस् \\ इति यथाङ्गं कल्पयित्वेष्टकां निदधाति मध्ये तूष्णीम् ॥
21.4.m: Having arranged [the bones] limb by limb with: 'May the wind be auspicious,' he places a brick in the middle silently;

21.4.d: प्रतिदिशम् अन्तेषु पराचीस् तिस्रस्तिस्रो ऽलक्षणाः पादमात्रीः ॥
21.4.m: in each direction at the borders, three each facing away, without marks, measuring a foot.

21.4.s: pradarāt purīṣam āhṛtya parikṛṣya vā sarvato 'purastāt //
21.4.d: प्रदरात् पुरीषम् आहृत्य परिकृष्य वा सर्वतो ऽपुरस्तात् ॥
21.4.m: Having brought earth from a cleft, or having dug around on all sides except the east;
The height is up to the mouth for a Brāhmaṇa;

21.4.s: avakābhiḥ kuśaiś ca prachādya parikṛṣṭaṃ ced yavān vapet //
21.4.d: अवकाभिः कुशैश् च प्रछाद्य परिकृष्टं चेद् यवान् वपेत् ॥
21.4.m: Having covered [it] with Avakā plants and Kuśa grass, if it was dug around, he should sow barley.

21.4.s: dakṣiṇataḥ kuṭile karṣū khātvā kṣīrodakābhyāṃ pūrayanti saptottarataḥ prācīr udakasya //
21.4.d: दक्षिणतः कुटिले कर्षू खात्वा क्षीरोदकाभ्यां पूरयन्ति सप्तोत्तरतः प्राचीर् उदकस्य ॥
21.4.m: To the south having dug curved furrows, they fill [them] with milk and water, and to the north seven [furrows] running east [with] water.
They throw in three stones each.
They cross over [them] with: 'Possessing stones.'
With: 'Wiping away evil,' they wipe themselves with Apāmārga plants.

21.4.s: sumitrayā nas \\ iti snātvāhatavāsaso 'naḍutpucham anvārabhya \\ anaḍvāham iti \\ ud vayam ity āgachanti //
21.4.d: सुमित्रया नस् \\ इति स्नात्वाहतवाससो ऽनडुत्पुछम् अन्वारभ्य \\ अनड्वाहम् इति \\ उद् वयम् इत्य् आगछन्ति ॥
21.4.m: Having bathed with: 'With a friendly [eye] may [the waters gaze upon] us,' dressed in unwashed garments, holding on to the tail of an ox with: 'The ox,' they return with: 'Upwards we [behold the light].'

21.4.s: grāmaśmaśānāntare maryādāloṣṭaṃ nidadhāti \\ imaṃ jīvebhyas \\ iti //
21.4.d: ग्रामश्मशानान्तरे मर्यादालोष्टं निदधाति \\ इमं जीवेभ्यस् \\ इति ॥
21.4.m: Between the village and the cremation ground, he places a boundary clod with: 'This [barrier] for the living.'

21.4.s: āñjanābhyañjane kṛtvaupāsanaṃ paristīrya vāraṇān paridhīn paridhāya vāraṇena sruveṇaikām āhutiṃ juhoti \\ agna āyūm̐ṣi \\ āyuṣmān agne \\ iti //
21.4.d: आञ्जनाभ्यञ्जने कृत्वौपासनं परिस्तीर्य वारणान् परिधीन् परिधाय वारणेन स्रुवेणैकाम् आहुतिं जुहोति \\ अग्न आयूम्̐षि \\ आयुष्मान् अग्ने \\ इति ॥
21.4.m: Having applied salve and ointment, having strewn around the domestic fire, and having set around enclosing sticks of Vāraṇa wood, he offers one oblation with a Vāraṇa dipping spoon with: 'O Agni, life-spans,' [and] 'Possessing long life, O Agni.'

21.4.s: athaiṣāṃ paridāṃ vadati parīme gām aneṣata \\ iti //
21.4.d: अथैषां परिदां वदति परीमे गाम् अनेषत \\ इति ॥
21.4.m: Then he recites their entrustment: 'Around these they have led the cow.'
By a non-door he removes the domestic fire with: 'The flesh-eater.'

21.4.s: āsandī sopadhānā dakṣiṇānaḍvān yavāś ca sarvaṃ purāṇam //
21.4.d: आसन्दी सोपधाना दक्षिणानड्वान् यवाश् च सर्वं पुराणम् ॥
21.4.m: A stool with a cushion, an ox, and barley constitute the sacrificial gift—all of it old.

22.1.m: A thousand [cows are] the sacrificial gift for the Abhijit;
For the Viśvajit, [it is] a thousand [cows] or all of one's possessions (sarvavedasa).

22.1.s: jyeṣṭhaṃ putram apabhajya bhūmiśūdravarjaṃ yogāviśeṣāt sarveṣām //
22.1.d: ज्येष्ठं पुत्रम् अपभज्य भूमिशूद्रवर्जं योगाविशेषात् सर्वेषाम् ॥
22.1.m: Having portioned out the eldest son, excluding land and Śūdras, because there is no distinction regarding the ownership of all.
Or the giving of a Śūdra is [permitted], because of textual mention and lack of contradiction.
Due to the absence of sacrificial substance, it ends there;
or [there is] completion [of the sacrifice], because the purifying bath (avabhṛtha) is enjoined by sacred text,
In the case of a fixed quantity, all [is given], because there is no specification.
Or [only] the excess [is given], in conformity with the archetype rite;

22.1.s: avabhṛthād udetya rohiṇyau vatsachavyau sakarṇapuchāvachāte paridadhāte //
22.1.d: अवभृथाद् उदेत्य रोहिण्यौ वत्सछव्यौ सकर्णपुछावछाते परिदधाते ॥
22.1.m: Having stepped out from the purifying bath, they put on two red skins of calves, with ears and tails attached, which have been unstitched.
He resides outside for twelve nights, carrying a spade just as [the sacrificer carrying] the fire-pan (ukhā),
at the Udumbara tree, he feeds on roots and fruits;
"Ordinary people" means a Vaiśya; "people of one's own standing" means a Rājanya, according to sacred text.
Among the Niṣādas, [he observes] abstention from cultivated food, and drinking from earthenware vessels.
he should not refuse what is given.
Or he may sacrifice with the twin [rites, the Abhijit and Viśvajit], the preceding and following [successively],
The two sacrificial grounds (devayajanas) are to the south and north.
The rites outside the altar (vedi) are common;
If there is a conflict of actions, the Abhijit takes precedence each time.
The sacrificial gift is a separate thousand [cows for each].

22.1.s: sarvajit samahāvrataḥ saṃvatsaradīkṣaḥ saptāhābhiṣavas tisra upasadaḥ ṣaḍ vā //
22.1.d: सर्वजित् समहाव्रतः संवत्सरदीक्षः सप्ताहाभिषवस् तिस्र उपसदः षड् वा ॥
22.1.m: The Sarvajit has the Mahāvrata, a year-long consecration, seven days of soma-pressing, and three or six Upasad days.

22.2.m: He gives a chariot drawn by one hundred horses to the Adhvaryu while the fire-altar is being piled;
At the time of the sacrificial gifts, [he gives] a thousand to all [the priests together].
There are four Sāhasra sacrifices, having a thousand [cows] as their sacrificial gift.
The Jyotis and the Viśvajyotis are equal to a three-day rite (trirātra).
The first is for those who desire heaven, those who desire cattle, or those who have rivals.
The sacrificial gift is a white horse with a gold ornament on its forehead;
There is no cessation of the archetypal [gift], because of its connection with the Udgātṛ priest.
The second [rite is performed] for those who have a chronic disease, who desire firm standing, or who desire food.
The sacrificial gift is twenty-one [cows] with a horse, or a horse.
The sacrificial gift is a hundred [cows] with a horse, or a horse.

22.2.s: yathādravye janapade yajeta teṣāṃ yathotsāhaṃ dadyāt //
22.2.d: यथाद्रव्ये जनपदे यजेत तेषां यथोत्साहं दद्यात् ॥
22.2.m: Whatever substances are in the country in which he sacrifices, he should give those according to his capacity.
Or [he gives] substitutes for all his possessions:
A milk-cow, an ox, a plough, grain, a storage jar, a pair of male and female slaves, a kitchen, a vehicle, a tent, and beds.

22.3.m: Where plants do not grow, that is the sacrificial ground.
The two pressing-boards are the naves of a hearse.
The animal offering during the soma pressing is red, for Agni accompanied by Rudra.
The officiating priests officiate wearing red garments and red turbans.

22.3.s: kāṇakhorakūṭabaṇḍā hrutamiśrā navanava dakṣiṇā dadāti liṅgānām //
22.3.d: काणखोरकूटबण्डा ह्रुतमिश्रा नवनव दक्षिणा ददाति लिङ्गानाम् ॥
22.3.m: He gives as sacrificial gift one-eyed, lame, hornless, tailless, and defective animals, nine of each, for each characteristic.
Or [nine] per person, because of the eligibility for giving.
Or bringing forward the archetypal [cows] in division.
At the time of the sacrificial gift, they should pierce them with thorns.
While they are distressed, [they take] the clarified butter of those that are not distressed.
The rules of the Sādhyaḥkras [apply], like that having a golden garland.
In the Ekatrika, the sacrificial gift is one hundred and sixty-six [cows].
Everything beginning with the consecration is performed on the same day.
Or a sacrificial cake is [offered] in place of the animal victim for Agni-Soma.
The Subrahmaṇyā chant ceases at the end of the omentum [offering].
The officiating priests dwell in each [cardinal] direction.
The others at distances decreased by one krośa each.
They convey them in four horse-chariots with leather bags of milk.
The [animal] for buying the soma is a three-year-old [bull] with testicles intact.
He occupies [a field of] ripe rice or barley.
It is a grain threshing-floor, according to common understanding.

22.3.s: ye vedim abhitas tān uttaravedideśe mṛdhnanti //
22.3.d: ये वेदिम् अभितस् तान् उत्तरवेदिदेशे मृध्नन्ति ॥
22.3.m: Those [sheaves] that are around the altar they thresh in the place of the high altar.
Or [it is] a heap of dust, because of the lack of distinction in understanding.
The threshing post is the sacrificial post, [or] the pole of a plough.
Because of the mention of ready-made [items], there is cessation of the archetypal [procedures].
Or arable land and the like [are the sacrificial gifts] of the second, because of proximity.

22.4.m: The Vrātyastomas are four.

22.4.s: vrātyagaṇasya ye sampādayeyus te prathamena yajeran //
22.4.d: व्रात्यगणस्य ये सम्पादयेयुस् ते प्रथमेन यजेरन् ॥
22.4.m: Those of a Vrātya group who can afford it should sacrifice with the first.
Censured and cruel [persons should sacrifice] with the second.

22.4.s: apetaprajananā sthavirās tadākhyās teṣāṃ yo nṛśam̐satamaḥ syād dravyavattamo vānūcānatamo vā tasya gārhapate dīkṣeran //
22.4.d: अपेतप्रजनना स्थविरास् तदाख्यास् तेषां यो नृशम्̐सतमः स्याद् द्रव्यवत्तमो वानूचानतमो वा तस्य गार्हपते दीक्षेरन् ॥
22.4.m: Those past procreative age, the elders, are designated by that name; among them, he who is the most cruel, or the wealthiest, or the most learned, at his Gārhapatya fire they should undergo consecration.
They should sit consuming [portions of soma] after his consumption.
There are Vrātya possessions.
A turban tied across, [and] a goad.
A jyāhroḍa—a bow unfit [for battle] is so designated.
Not black, or with black borders, is so designated.
A rough cart covered with planks.

22.4.s: aśvāśvatarābhyāṃ kamprābhyāṃ yuktaḥ syād ity eke //
22.4.d: अश्वाश्वतराभ्यां कम्प्राभ्यां युक्तः स्याद् इत्य् एके ॥
22.4.m: It should be yoked with a horse and a mule that are skittish, say some.
Two sheepskins with flanks attached, black and white.
In the same manner the skins belong to the others.

22.4.s: dāmatūṣāṇi balūkāntāni dvicūḍānyāvikāni vāsām̐si lohitāntāni kṛṣṇāntāni vā tadākhyāni //
22.4.d: दामतूषाणि बलूकान्तानि द्विचूडान्याविकानि वासाम्̐सि लोहितान्तानि कृष्णान्तानि वा तदाख्यानि ॥
22.4.m: Woollen garments with fringed cords, ending in tassels, with two crests, red-bordered or black-bordered, are so designated.

22.4.s: dāmanī dvedve upānahau ca karṇinyau kṛṣṇe syātām ity eke //
22.4.d: दामनी द्वेद्वे उपानहौ च कर्णिन्यौ कृष्णे स्याताम् इत्य् एके ॥
22.4.m: Two ropes each, and two shoes with ears, black, should be [theirs], say some.
At the time of the sacrificial gift, they should give the Vrātya possessions to a degraded Brahmin of the Māgadha region.
Or to those who have not ceased from Vrātya conduct.
Because of the Vedic text: "Wiping off [guilt] upon them indeed, they go forth."
They should each give thirty-three [cows as] sacrificial gifts.
The householder [gives] double, say some.
Having sacrificed with a Vrātyastoma, they should cease from Vrātya-hood.
The Agniṣṭut is for those desiring spiritual lustre, valour, food, [or] firm standing, and for one who considers himself as if unpurified.
Or [for one desiring that priests] should not fall away from him.

22.5.m: The particular [chant variations are] in the Chāndogya [tradition], according to desire.
He should give according to capacity among things sacred to Agni: an ox, gold, a horse, [or] goats.
The first has an unexpressed morning pressing.
The sacrificial gift is a horse-drawn chariot yoked with four, one of them dark brown.
The Bṛhaspatisava is for one desiring fiery energy, spiritual lustre, [or] priesthood.
He pours out the Devasū oblations.

22.5.s: atigrāhyavad grahaṃ gṛhṇāti bṛhaspate ati yad aryas \\ iti //
22.5.d: अतिग्राह्यवद् ग्रहं गृह्णाति बृहस्पते अति यद् अर्यस् \\ इति ॥
22.5.m: He draws a soma cup like an Atigrāhya cup with: "O Bṛhaspati, that which [exceeds] the rival..."
The animal to be seized belongs to Bṛhaspati.

22.5.s: nihiteṣu nārāśam̐seṣu prātaḥsavane 'napākurvann ekādaśa dakṣiṇā vyādiśati //
22.5.d: निहितेषु नाराशम्̐सेषु प्रातःसवने ऽनपाकुर्वन्न् एकादश दक्षिणा व्यादिशति ॥
22.5.m: When the Nārāśaṃsa cups have been deposited at the morning pressing, without leading [them] away, he assigns eleven sacrificial gifts.
At the midday [pressing], twelve, with a horse [as the twelfth].
The leading away takes place at the end of the omentum oblation of the Anūbandhyā cow.
And the crossing over of all [the cows].
Or there should be eleven hundred each.
A horse, however, is additional at the midday [soma pressing].
He is consecrated with clarified butter on a black antelope skin in the manner of the Vājapeya.
Or with the residue of the Śukra and Manthin cups.

22.5.s: sarājāno brāhmaṇā yaṃ puraskurvīrant sa etena yajeta //
22.5.d: सराजानो ब्राह्मणा यं पुरस्कुर्वीरन्त् स एतेन यजेत ॥
22.5.m: He whom the Brāhmaṇas, together with kings, place at their head, should sacrifice with this [rite].

22.6.m: The Sarvasvāra has cooked food for sacrificial gifts.
Beginning from the consecration, he only smells the portions to be consumed.
The disposal into water is for the non-soma portions.

22.6.s: ārbhave stūyamāne dakṣiṇenaudumbarīṃ kṛṣṇājine saṃviśati dakṣiṇāśirāḥ //
22.6.d: आर्भवे स्तूयमाने दक्षिणेनौदुम्बरीं कृष्णाजिने संविशति दक्षिणाशिराः ॥
22.6.m: While the Ārbhava [stotra] is being chanted, he lies down south of the audumbarī post on a black antelope skin with his head toward the south.

22.6.s: tad eva mriyate jīvec ced dairghaśravasam̐ svāsu yajñāyajñiyasthāne kuryuḥ //
22.6.d: तद् एव म्रियते जीवेच् चेद् दैर्घश्रवसम्̐ स्वासु यज्ञायज्ञियस्थाने कुर्युः ॥
22.6.m: He dies right then; if he should live, they should perform the Dairghaśravasa [sāman] on its own verses in place of the Yajñāyajñīya.
When he is dead, it ends right there, because of the absence of need.
Having thrown the sacrificer’s utensils, soma residue, and oblations into the Āhavanīya fire, they may go according to their purpose.
Or there is completion [of the sacrifice], because both are enjoined.

22.6.s: samiṣṭayajurante saṃ tvā hinvanti \\ iti dārvāharaṇam //
22.6.d: समिष्टयजुरन्ते सं त्वा हिन्वन्ति \\ इति दार्वाहरणम् ॥
22.6.m: At the conclusion of the samiṣṭayajus offerings, bringing of the wood takes place with: 'They speed thee…'
The fashioning [of the litter takes place] with: 'They have fashioned thee…'
The washing [takes place] with: 'They cleanse thee…'
The weaving of the chair-litter [takes place] with: 'They sharpen thee…'

22.6.s: āsandyainam avabhṛtham̐ hṛtvābhyukṣya somopanahanena prachādyānūbandhyavapāhomānte dakṣiṇasyāṃ vediśroṇau sarvakeśaśmaśrulomavapanam //
22.6.d: आसन्द्यैनम् अवभृथम्̐ हृत्वाभ्युक्ष्य सोमोपनहनेन प्रछाद्यानूबन्ध्यवपाहोमान्ते दक्षिणस्यां वेदिश्रोणौ सर्वकेशश्मश्रुलोमवपनम् ॥
22.6.m: Having carried him on the chair-litter to the final bath, sprinkled [him] with water, covered [him] with the soma-cloth, and concluded the offering of the omentum of the anūbandhyā cow, the shaving of all hair of the head, beard, and body [takes place] on the southern buttock of the vedi.

22.6.s: anūbandhyānte 'gnīn āhṛtya vedimadhyam āgnīdhrād dakṣiṇaṃ dakṣiṇāśirasaṃ citāv āhitam udgātā trir yāmena parigāyan nāke suparṇam ity etasyām //
22.6.d: अनूबन्ध्यान्ते ऽग्नीन् आहृत्य वेदिमध्यम् आग्नीध्राद् दक्षिणं दक्षिणाशिरसं चिताव् आहितम् उद्गाता त्रिर् यामेन परिगायन् नाके सुपर्णम् इत्य् एतस्याम् ॥
22.6.m: At the conclusion of the anūbandhyā, having brought the fires to the middle of the vedi, to the south of the Āgnīdhra [hearth], when he has been placed on the pyre with his head to the south, the Udgātṛ chants thrice around [him] with the Yāma [sāman] on this [verse]: 'The fair-winged bird on the firmament…'

22.6.s: dhūmaprāptam \\ tveṣas te dhūma ṛṇvati \\ iti //
22.6.d: धूमप्राप्तम् \\ त्वेषस् ते धूम ऋण्वति \\ इति ॥
22.6.m: When the smoke reaches him, with: 'Fierce does thy smoke rise…'

22.6.s: agniprāptam agne mṛḍa mahā3ṃ asi \\ ity anyatareṇa //
22.6.d: अग्निप्राप्तम् अग्ने मृड महा3ं असि \\ इत्य् अन्यतरेण ॥
22.6.m: When the fire reaches him, with either: 'O Agni, be gracious; thou art great3…'
Or [the funeral rites take place] at the end of the concluding bath (udavasanīyā), because of the completion of everything.
If he should live, he should seek to die by this very undertaking.
The Ṛtvigapohanīya rites are three.
And the two final days of the Chandoma [period] having been separated.
The Pṛṣṭhyastomas are: Trivṛt, Pañcadaśa, Saptadaśa, Ekaviṃśa, Triṇava, and Trayastriṃśa.

22.7.s: cāturmāsyāḥ somās triṣu parvasthāneṣu pārṣṭhikāni pṛṣṭhyo vihṛta iti śruteḥ //
22.7.d: चातुर्मास्याः सोमास् त्रिषु पर्वस्थानेषु पार्ष्ठिकानि पृष्ठ्यो विहृत इति श्रुतेः ॥
22.7.m: The soma rites of the Cāturmāsyas consist of the Pṛṣṭhya [days] distributed at three seasonal joints, because of the śruti: 'The Pṛṣṭhya is distributed.'
In place of the Vaiśvadeva [parvan] is the first.
And the preparation of the high altar is omitted.
The animal is tied to an enclosing stick.
In the second [parvan] is a two-day rite named Dvidiva.
Some say the first is an Agniṣṭoma.
In the third [parvan] is a three-day rite; the last day is an Atirātra.
Some say the first is an Agniṣṭoma.
A Jyotiṣṭoma takes the place of the Śunāsīrīya [parvan].
At five [soma pressings], the pressing animals are those for the Viśvedevas, Varuṇa, the Maruts, Agni, and Indra-Agni.

22.7.s: pañcāśataṃpañcāśataṃ pratyahaṃ dadāty uttame dvādaśam̐ śatam //
22.7.d: पञ्चाशतंपञ्चाशतं प्रत्यहं ददात्य् उत्तमे द्वादशम्̐ शतम् ॥
22.7.m: He gives fifty [cows] each day; on the last day, one hundred and twelve.
Or fifty calves born according to the season.
Between the joints, he wears an unwashed garment.
The barren cows (anūbandhyā) are dedicated to Bṛhaspati, Mitra-Varuṇa, Sūrya, and the Aśvins respectively, according to each concluding bath.
[Namely, for] the Agnyādheya, Punarādheya, Agnihotra, New- and Full-Moon sacrifices, Dākṣāyaṇa, and Āgrayaṇa rites.
Some say the animal sacrifice is an Ukthya.

22.8.m: In the morning, he pours out the oblations following the pressing animals.
The savanīya [offerings] have as their first the deity of the final offering, [namely] the anūbandhyā [cow].
The unexpressed Upahavya is for one desiring a domain.
Or for one falsely accused [of a grave sin].

22.8.d: श्यावो ऽश्वो दक्षिणा तं ब्रह्मणे ददाति ॥
22.8.m: A dark horse is the sacrificial gift; he gives it to the Brahman priest.
The Ṛtapeya is for one desiring heaven.
or in both cases there is a count of twelve, on account of being an auxiliary [specification].

22.8.s: camasaṃ pūrṇam aṅguliparvaṇā maulyena sarvataḥ pramitam ādyāyām upasadi //
22.8.d: चमसं पूर्णम् अङ्गुलिपर्वणा मौल्येन सर्वतः प्रमितम् आद्यायाम् उपसदि ॥
22.8.m: On the first Upasad day, a full cup measured all around by the joint of a finger as the purchase-price.
About to consume [the soma], they should speak the truth.
A soma cup made of udumbara wood is to be given as the sacrificial gift to a Brahman priest of the same gotra.
[It is filled] from the pūtabhṛt [vat], because it serves all purposes.

22.8.s: am̐śucamasam eke tena sa yajeteti śruteḥ //
22.8.d: अम्̐शुचमसम् एके तेन स यजेतेति श्रुतेः ॥
22.8.m: Some [prescribe] an am̐śu cup, because of the Vedic text: 'With that he should sacrifice.'
The Dvināmottara, the Bahuhiraṇya, and the Dūṇāśa [follow].

22.9.m: At the dīkṣaṇīyā offering he gives gold of twelve measures.
And at each subsequent [rite], double the previous one:
at the prāyaṇīyā, atithyā, and the Upasads;
at the end of the omentum of the animal [sacrifice], and when the savanamukhīya [cups] are deposited at each pressing;
at the udayanīyā, at the anūbandhyā, and at the udavasānīyā, and a garland to the Udgātṛ priest;
a golden ornament to the Hotṛ priest, and a hundred oxen to all [the priests] at the proper time.
The Vaiśyastoma is for a Vaiśya and for one desiring cattle.
At the morning pressing, the mixture is made with freshly drawn milk;
The sacrificial gifts are five-year-old spotted young bulls.

22.9.s: vatsataryaś ca trihāyaṇyo 'pravītāḥ pañcavarṇā rājīvapṛśnayo navanītaprāśnayo 'ruṇāḥ piśaṅgyaḥ sāraṅgya iti //
22.9.d: वत्सतर्यश् च त्रिहायण्यो ऽप्रवीताः पञ्चवर्णा राजीवपृश्नयो नवनीतप्राश्नयो ऽरुणाः पिशङ्ग्यः सारङ्ग्य इति ॥
22.9.m: And heifers, three years old, unbred, five-coloured: striped-spotted, butter-eating, reddish, yellowish-brown, and speckled.
A thousand of both, or one hundred and twelve.
The Tīvrasut is an Ukthya for one excessively purged by soma;
or for those suffering from chronic disease, desiring a domain, desiring offspring, or desiring cattle.

22.10.m: They milk a hundred cows for the admixture.
Consuming [takes place] during the individual portions of the Achāvāka;

22.10.s: teṣv evonnayanam abhyabhi somān unnayantīti śruteḥ //
22.10.d: तेष्व् एवोन्नयनम् अभ्यभि सोमान् उन्नयन्तीति श्रुतेः ॥
22.10.m: Drawing [the soma] takes place into those [cups] alone, because of the Vedic text: 'They draw the soma portions over and over.'

22.10.s: adhvaryū camasādhvaryavaś ca sarve pratigṛṇanty achāvākāya //
22.10.d: अध्वर्यू चमसाध्वर्यवश् च सर्वे प्रतिगृणन्त्य् अछावाकाय ॥
22.10.m: The Adhvaryu and all the Camasādhvaryus respond to the Achāvāka.
The first of the paired rites is the Rāṭ, for a noble desiring kingship.
He should give according to his ability groups of twenty-one [cows].
A bull for Indra is the supplementary animal sacrifice.
He should give according to his ability groups of ten [cows].
An animal for Agni is the supplementary animal sacrifice.
The Aupaśada is for one desiring procreation.
The sacrificial gift is one hundred and twenty-four [cows].
An animal for the Viśvedevas is the supplementary animal sacrifice.

22.10.s: bahu pratigṛhya garagīriva yo manyeta tasya punastoma ukthyaḥ //
22.10.d: बहु प्रतिगृह्य गरगीरिव यो मन्येत तस्य पुनस्तोम उक्थ्यः ॥
22.10.m: For one who, having accepted many gifts, considers himself as if he had swallowed poison, his [sacrifice] is the Punastoma, an Ukthya.
The sacrificial gift is twelve pairs, and of [cows] having returned [to milk], according to ability.
The two sacrifices for one desiring cattle are Catuṣṭomas.

22.10.s: pūrvasmin yathāśakty ekaśaphān dadyād ubhayān uttarasmin //
22.10.d: पूर्वस्मिन् यथाशक्त्य् एकशफान् दद्याद् उभयान् उत्तरस्मिन् ॥
22.10.m: At the first, he should give single-hoofed animals according to his ability; at the second, both [single-hoofed and cloven-hoofed].
And the Udbhid and Balabhid are connected rites bringing [their fruits].
Having sacrificed with the first, [he] necessarily [sacrifices] with the second.
Between these two there is an Iṣu offering, [which is] a cake on eight potsherds for Agni.
The enclosing sticks are tipped with arrows.
For half a month, a month, or a year [between them].
The sacrificial gift consists of groups of twenty-four according to the Gāyatrī measure, or according to ability.
For one desirous of honor, there are the two Apaciti rites.
The sacrificial gift is a horse chariot yoked with four horses on both [sides].
They are accompanied by the piling of the fire altar, are Agniṣṭomas, and have the consecration of the Sarvajit.
The first has wings; the second is the Jyotis.

22.11.m: The sacrificial gifts are four cartloads of grain each.
For the first, [wagons drawn by] six oxen; for the second, [wagons drawn by] four oxen.
The sacrificial gift is a thousand bulls, or one hundred and twelve.
The Gosava is an Ukthya with a sacrificial gift of ten thousand [cows].

22.11.s: sarājāno viśo yaṃ puraskurvīrant sa etena yajeta //
22.11.d: सराजानो विशो यं पुरस्कुर्वीरन्त् स एतेन यजेत ॥
22.11.m: One whom the subjects together with their kings place at their head should sacrifice with this.
With warm fresh milk to the south of the Āhavanīya fire.
They should address him as 'Sthapati' (Chief).

22.11.s: vaiśyastomadakṣiṇāliṅgo marutstomo gaṇayajño bhrātṝṇām̐ sakhīnāṃ vā //
22.11.d: वैश्यस्तोमदक्षिणालिङ्गो मरुत्स्तोमो गणयज्ञो भ्रातॄणाम्̐ सखीनां वा ॥
22.11.m: The Marutstoma, having the sacrificial gift characteristic of the Vaiśyastoma, is a collective sacrifice for brothers or friends.
For one desirous of offspring or cattle, there is the Aindrāgnakulāya, whose sacrificial gift is a herd.
It is a dual sacrifice for two brothers or two friends.
The Indrastoma is a sacrifice for a king.
For one desirous of the office of family priest, there is the Indrāgnyoḥ Stoma.
Or for a king and a family priest sacrificing together.
The sacrificial gift conforms to the Gāyatrī for a Brāhmaṇa.
[The gifts] conform to the Bṛhatī for one desirous of cattle.
For one practicing sorcery, they are well-known.
The Saṃdaṃśa and the Vajra are for one practicing sorcery.
A cow whose horns are trimmed or red-eared is the soma-purchasing cow of the Ṣoḍaśin.
He should practice sorcery against a single king with the first.
Or he may employ the two alternately.

22.11.s: śamitvā stṛtvā vā jyotiṣṭomena yajeta śāntyarthena //
22.11.d: शमित्वा स्तृत्वा वा ज्योतिष्टोमेन यजेत शान्त्यर्थेन ॥
22.11.m: Having appeased or slain [the enemy], he should sacrifice with the Jyotiṣṭoma for the purpose of expiation.

23.1.m: Ahīna sacrifices have twelve Upasad days and are completed within a month.
The consecrations occupy the remainder of the soma-pressing and Upasad days.
They begin with two-day rites and extend up to twelve-day rites.
Some hold that Atirātras also [are included] on account of being mentioned there.
The days of the Ten-Day rite [are used] in the two-day rites and so on with an increase of one [each time], because their qualities are observed.
In the four-day rites and beyond, [it is] more.
He gives them equally divided each day.
The first four are without the Ṣoḍaśin.
The Navasaptadaśa [Atirātra] is for one desiring progeny.
The Viṣuvant is for the eldest son of an eldest wife.
The Āyuḥ is for one desiring heaven, or for one who is chronically ill.
The Jyotiṣṭoma, Viśvajit, Trivṛt, Pañcadaśa, Saptadaśa, and Ekavim̐śa [Atirātras] are respectively for those desiring prosperity, livestock, sacred luster, vigor, food, and stability.
The Aptoryāma is for one from whom livestock are about to perish entirely.
The Abhijit is for one having rivals.
The Sarvastoma is for one desiring to become prosperous.

23.2.m: The Atirātras of the latter two are without the Ṣoḍaśin.
[They are] the Āṅgirasa, Caitraratha, and Kāpivana.
Some [teachers hold that] the second has an Ukthya preceding [the Atirātra].

23.2.s: prathamena yajeta yaḥ pauṇyo hīna iva syāt //
23.2.d: प्रथमेन यजेत यः पौण्यो हीन इव स्यात् ॥
23.2.m: He who is lacking in merit, as it were, should sacrifice with the first.
One desiring heaven or one desiring livestock [should sacrifice] with the third.
There are five three-day rites: the Garga, Baida, Chandoma, Antarvasu, and Parāka.
In the second, all the Atirātras are nine-versed.
The Antarvasu is for one desiring livestock.
The Parāka is for one desiring heaven.
The Atri-caturvīra, Jāmadagnya, Vasiṣṭha-sam̐sarpa, and Viśvāmitra.
The Jāmadagnya has twenty consecrations, [and is] for one desiring nourishment.
Its Upasad rites are provided with cake offerings.
[The offering has] the characteristics of clarified butter, because of taking its place;
or it has the characteristics of vegetable food, on account of the common substance.

At each Upasad, with an increase of one potsherd, beginning from a single-potsherd [cake, there are cakes] for Agni, the Aśvins, Viṣṇu, Soma, Savitṛ, Dhātṛ, the Maruts, Bṛhaspati, Mitra-Varuṇa, Indra, and the Viśvedevas.

23.3.s: teṣām̐ homaḥ agne ver hotraṃ ver adhvaram \ ā pitaraṃ vaiśvānaram avase kar \ indrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā \ devāv aśvinau madhukaśayādyemaṃ yajñaṃ yajamānāya mimikṣatam \ indrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā \ deva viṣṇa urv adyāsmin yajñe yajamānāyādhi vikramasva \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā \ deva soma retodhā adyāsmin yajñe yajamānāyaidhi \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā \ deva savitaḥ susāvitram adyāsmin yajñe yajamānāyāsuvasva \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā \ deva dhātaḥ sudhātādyāsmin yajñe yajamānāyaidhi \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā \ devā grāvāṇo madhumatīm adyāsmin yajñe yajamānāya vācaṃ vadata \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā \ devy anumate 'nv adyemaṃ yajñaṃ yajamānāya manyasva \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā \ devy adite svādityam adyāsmin yajñe yajamānāyāsuvasva \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā \ devya āpo naṃnamyadhvam adyāsmin yajñe yajamānāya \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā \ sadaḥsadaḥ prajāvān ṛbhur juṣāṇas \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā \ deva tvaṣṭaḥ suretodhā adyāsmin yajñe yajamānāyaidhi \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā \\ iti //
23.3.d: तेषाम्̐ होमः अग्ने वेर् होत्रं वेर् अध्वरम् \ आ पितरं वैश्वानरम् अवसे कर् \ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुता हविः स्वाहा \ देवाव् अश्विनौ मधुकशयाद्येमं यज्ञं यजमानाय मिमिक्षतम् \ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुता हविः स्वाहा \ देव विष्ण उर्व् अद्यास्मिन् यज्ञे यजमानायाधि विक्रमस्व \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुता हविः स्वाहा \ देव सोम रेतोधा अद्यास्मिन् यज्ञे यजमानायैधि \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुता हविः स्वाहा \ देव सवितः सुसावित्रम् अद्यास्मिन् यज्ञे यजमानायासुवस्व \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुता हविः स्वाहा \ देव धातः सुधाताद्यास्मिन् यज्ञे यजमानायैधि \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुता हविः स्वाहा \ देवा ग्रावाणो मधुमतीम् अद्यास्मिन् यज्ञे यजमानाय वाचं वदत \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुता हविः स्वाहा \ देव्य् अनुमते ऽन्व् अद्येमं यज्ञं यजमानाय मन्यस्व \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुता हविः स्वाहा \ देव्य् अदिते स्वादित्यम् अद्यास्मिन् यज्ञे यजमानायासुवस्व \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुता हविः स्वाहा \ देव्य आपो नंनम्यध्वम् अद्यास्मिन् यज्ञे यजमानाय \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुता हविः स्वाहा \ सदःसदः प्रजावान् ऋभुर् जुषाणस् \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुता हविः स्वाहा \ देव त्वष्टः सुरेतोधा अद्यास्मिन् यज्ञे यजमानायैधि \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुता हविः स्वाहा \\ इति ॥
23.3.m: Their offering [formulae are]: 'Agni, foster the office of Hotṛ, foster the sacrifice; take father Vaiśvānara for help! For Indra, for the gods, offer the oblation, svāhā!' 'Divine Aśvins, moisten today this sacrifice for the sacrificer with your honey-whip! For Indra, for the gods, offer the oblation, svāhā!' 'Divine Viṣṇu, stride widely today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer! For Indra, for the gods, offer the oblation, svāhā!' 'Divine Soma, be the placer of seed today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer! For Indra, for the gods, offer the oblation, svāhā!' 'Divine Savitṛ, impel good impulsion today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer! For Indra, for the gods, offer the oblation, svāhā!' 'Divine Dhātṛ, be a good supporter today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer! For Indra, for the gods, offer the oblation, svāhā!' 'Divine pressing-stones, speak honeyed speech today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer! For Indra, for the gods, offer the oblation, svāhā!' 'Divine Anumati, approve today this sacrifice for the sacrificer! For Indra, for the gods, offer the oblation, svāhā!' 'Divine Aditi, grant freedom from injury today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer! For Indra, for the gods, offer the oblation, svāhā!' 'Divine Waters, bend low today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer! For Indra, for the gods, offer the oblation, svāhā!' 'Delighting at every place, possessing progeny, Ṛbhu... For Indra, for the gods, offer the oblation, svāhā!' 'Divine Tvaṣṭṛ, be the placer of good seed today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer! For Indra, for the gods, offer the oblation, svāhā!'—thus.
With these, at the end of the pressing, he sacrifices for twelve days in reverse order, with one [oblation] each day.

23.4.s: tena yakṣyamāṇaḥ pañca varṣāṇy āśvayujīśukleṣu catustrim̐śataṃ paśūn ālabhate mārutān //
23.4.d: तेन यक्ष्यमाणः पञ्च वर्षाण्य् आश्वयुजीशुक्लेषु चतुस्त्रिम्̐शतं पशून् आलभते मारुतान् ॥
23.4.m: Intending to sacrifice with this, for five years during the bright fortnights of the month of Āśvayuja, he seizes thirty-four animal victims for the Maruts,
having the marks of the sacrificial gifts of the Vaiśyastoma;
bulls and heifers, in order of color.
Having carried fire around them, they release the bulls, and conclude [the rite] with the heifers.
In this manner, they tether the bulls for five years.

23.4.d: षष्ठे सवनीया भवन्ति त्रयस्त्रयो ऽन्वहम् ऐन्द्रामारुताः ॥
23.4.m: In the sixth year, they become the pressing animals, three each day for Indra and the Maruts.

23.4.s: yaḥ kāmayeta bahuḥ syām iti sa etena yajeta //
23.4.d: यः कामयेत बहुः स्याम् इति स एतेन यजेत ॥
23.4.m: One who desires, 'May I become manifold,' should sacrifice with this.
one to Bṛhaspati if it loses a horn, has deformed horns, or is one-eyed;
to Agni accompanied by Rudra, if it is afflicted by Rudra;
if it is crushed, a single-potsherd cake to the Earth;
if it is carried off by force, [a cake] to Indra the Forceful;
if it dies when it is fit for food, a twelve-potsherd cake to Prajāpati.
He should feed the dead animal to Brahmins.
Throwing into water or depositing [the food takes place], because it is spoiled.
Elsewhere too, because of the connection with a defect.
[The days are] Jyotis, Go, Mahāvrata, Go, and Āyus.
The Ahīna sacrifices have the [Mahā]vrata and have the Sarvajit consecrations.

23.5.m: There are three six-day rites; the first is for the seasons.
In the second, there is a five-day rite having the Bṛhadrathantara-pṛṣṭha, named Pṛṣṭhyāvalamba.
In the third, after three [days], there are the Trikadruka days.
There are seven seven-day rites; the first four have the [Mahā]vrata as the final [day].
From the second onward, there are six one-day rites.
[In] the seven-day rite of Janaka, after four [days], there are the Viśvajit and the Mahāvrata.
In the final [seven-day rite], there is a six-day rite having the Bṛhadrathantara-pṛṣṭha, named Pṛṣṭhyastoma.
In the eight-day rite, the Mahāvrata follows the six-day rite.
In the nine-day rite, there are the Trikadruka days.
The second [nine-day rite consists of] the Pṛṣṭhyāvalamba after the Trikadruka days.
An Ukthya having Agniṣṭoma wings is repeated thrice.
The Pūrdaśarātra is for one against whom black magic is being practiced.
It has an Ukthya with Agniṣṭoma wings,
The Chandomadaśāha is for one desiring cattle.
Following the Pṛṣṭhyāvalamba, there are four Chandomas.
The Pauṇḍarīka is for one desiring all prosperity.
It is a ten-day rite without rising from a sacrificial session.
The duty of the Adhvaryu is identical in the Atirātras, except for the Viśvajit.

24.1.m: The night sacrificial sessions begin with the twelve-day rite.
They end with forty [days], increasing by one.
When [the number] is not filled out, the ten-day rite is subsequent.
In rites prescribed according to the archetype, the Mahāvrata follows the ten-day rite when there is need for a one-day rite.
When there is need for a five-day rite, its first five [days are used].

24.1.s: tryahārthe jyotir gaur āyur iti trikadrukāḥ //
24.1.d: त्र्यहार्थे ज्योतिर् गौर् आयुर् इति त्रिकद्रुकाः ॥
24.1.m: When there is need for a three-day rite, the Trikadrukas, namely Jyotis, Go, and Āyus [are used].
When there is need for a four-day rite, [these] and the [Mahā]vrata as prescribed [are used].
The interval between the Atirātras is the place for insertion.
Among those that are brought together by insertion, the smaller and smaller [rite comes] first.
There are two thirteen-day rites: after the Pṛṣṭhya, there is a Sarvastoma Atirātra.
The second is prescribed according to the archetype.
There are three fourteen-day rites.
In the middle one, the Trikadruka days are on both sides of the Pṛṣṭhya.
This rite is for those whose marriage, water offerings, or bed-sharing are in dispute.
The third is enjoined according to the archetype rite.
There are four fifteen-day rites.
The first two are explained by the two fourteen-day rites.
Between the two Pṛṣṭhya [six-day periods] is the Mahāvrata.
After the Atirātra, the Agniṣṭut of the second [rite is performed].
That [Agniṣṭut] is the opening rite of the third.

24.2.m: Prior to the twenty-day rite, [the multi-day rites] are enjoined according to the archetype rite.
In the twenty-day rite, there are an Abhiplava [six-day period], and the Abhijit and Viśvajit.
In the two twenty-one-day rites, the two Atirātras are without the Ṣoḍaśin.
There are three Abhiplavas; after the first, there is an Atirātra.
The second [twenty-one-day rite is performed] in summer for those who desire spiritual luster.

24.2.s: trayastrayaḥ svarasāmāno viṣuvantam abhitaḥ pṛṣṭhyau ca //
24.2.d: त्रयस्त्रयः स्वरसामानो विषुवन्तम् अभितः पृष्ठ्यौ च ॥
24.2.m: There are three Svarasāman days on each side of the central day, and two Pṛṣṭhya [six-day periods].
[The victim] dedicated to Soma and Pūṣan is to be offered.
Up to the thirty-two-day rite, [the rites] are enjoined according to the archetype rite.
The twenty-two-day rite is for those who desire food.
The twenty-three-day rite is for those who desire a firm standing.
The former twenty-four-day rite is for those who desire offspring or desire cattle.
The three subsequent Pṛṣṭhya days are in reverse and direct order.
On either side of it are two unexpressed Agniṣṭomas.
From that [follow] two unexpressed Agniṣṭomas.

24.2.s: pañcavim̐śatirātram annādyakāmānām̐ ṣaḍvim̐śatirātraṃ pratiṣṭhākāmānām̐ saptavim̐śatirātram ṛddhikāmānām aṣṭāvim̐śatirātraṃ prajākāmānāṃ paśukāmānāṃ vā //
24.2.d: पञ्चविम्̐शतिरात्रम् अन्नाद्यकामानाम्̐ षड्विम्̐शतिरात्रं प्रतिष्ठाकामानाम्̐ सप्तविम्̐शतिरात्रम् ऋद्धिकामानाम् अष्टाविम्̐शतिरात्रं प्रजाकामानां पशुकामानां वा ॥
24.2.m: The twenty-five-day rite is for those who desire food; the twenty-six-day rite is for those who desire a firm standing; the twenty-seven-day rite is for those who desire prosperity; the twenty-eight-day rite is for those who desire offspring or desire cattle.
There are three thirty-three-day rites.
After three [five-day periods], there is an Atirātra; [the other day is] the Viśvajit.
The second [thirty-three-day rite] contains the Vrata and three Abhiplavas.
In the intervals between the Abhiplavas, there are two Atirātras.
In the third, there are three five-day periods on each side of the Viśvajit.
Up to the forty-day rite, [the rites] are enjoined according to the archetype rite.
The thirty-four-day rite is for those who desire food.
The thirty-six-day rite is for those who desire a firm standing.
The thirty-seven-day rite is for those who desire prosperity.
The thirty-eight-day rite is for those who desire offspring or desire cattle.
The subsequent rites contain the Vrata, with the exception of the first and the third; there are seven forty-nine-day rites.

24.3.m: The first three-day period is the Kausurubinda.
And on either side of the Pṛṣṭhya [six-day period] there are twelve [days] each.
In the intervals between the groups, there are Atirātras.
There are two Abhiplavas, the Go and Āyus days, and two Atirātras.
There are two Abhiplavas, the Abhijit and Viśvajit, and two Atirātras.
There is an Abhiplava, an all-stoma [rite], nine [chants], seventeen [chants], and two Atirātras.
In the Āñjanābhyañjanīya, there are six Abhiplavas.
After four [Abhiplavas], there is an all-stoma Atirātra.

24.3.s: tasminn upasatsu sarpir vipaceyur gārhapatye gulgulusugandhitejanapītudārubhiḥ //
